title: Procedural Snake Slithering Locomotion System
prompt:
Create a single HTML file with a procedural snake slithering locomotion system using Three.js. The snake moves across a ground plane using sinusoidal body wave propagation, and a collectible amber artifact (loaded from a GLB model) is placed in the scene for the snake to pursue.

SCENE SETUP:
- Use a perspective camera at position (0, 12, 18) looking at the origin.
- Add a directional light at (5, 15, 10) with intensity 1.2 and an ambient light with intensity 0.4.
- Create a large ground plane (60x60) with a dark green color (#2a5a1a) and a subtle grid overlay.
- Add OrbitControls for camera interaction.
- Load 'MosquitoInAmber.glb' using GLTFLoader from a CDN (https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.163.0/examples/jsm/loaders/GLTFLoader.js). Scale the loaded model to fit roughly 1.5 units and place it at position (8, 0.5, 5). This is the collectible amber artifact. Add a slow Y-axis rotation animation to it and a subtle golden point light (color #ffcc44, intensity 2, distance 5) at its position.

SNAKE CONSTRUCTION:
- Build the snake from 20 spherical segments. The head segment has radius 0.45 and each subsequent segment decreases slightly in radius down to 0.2 for the tail.
- Color the head segment dark red (#8b0000). Body segments alternate between (#2d5a1e) and (#3a7a28). The last 3 tail segments taper and use (#4a8a38).
- Add two small white sphere eyes on the head segment with tiny black pupil spheres.
- Position all segments initially along the X-axis spaced 0.7 units apart starting from origin.

SLITHERING LOCOMOTION:
- Implement sinusoidal wave-based locomotion. The snake's body follows a sine wave pattern: lateral offset = amplitude * sin(frequency * segmentIndex - phase). The phase advances over time to create the traveling wave effect.
- Default parameters: amplitude = 1.5, frequency = 0.6, speed = 3.0 (units/sec), waveSpeed = 4.0 (phase advance rate).
- The head leads the direction of travel. Each body segment follows the position of the segment ahead of it with a slight delay (follow-the-leader with wave modulation).
- The snake's heading direction is controlled by the user (see interactions).

USER INTERACTIONS:
- LEFT/RIGHT arrow keys: steer the snake's heading direction. Turning rate = 2.0 radians/sec.
- UP/DOWN arrow keys: increase/decrease movement speed. Speed clamps between 0.5 and 8.0. Step = 0.5 per key press.
- SPACE key: toggle pause/resume of the entire locomotion system.
- 'W' key: toggle wave amplitude between normal (1.5) and exaggerated (3.0) for visual debugging.
- 'R' key: reset the snake to its initial position and heading (heading=0, position at origin, speed=3.0, amplitude=1.5).

DOM HUD:
- Create a HUD panel (top-left, semi-transparent dark background, white text, 14px monospace font) showing:
  - Current speed (1 decimal)
  - Current heading in degrees (1 decimal)
  - Wave amplitude
  - Paused status (YES/NO)
  - Distance to amber (distance from snake head to the amber model, 1 decimal)
  - Segments count
  - Frame count (increments each animation frame when not paused)

COLLECTION MECHANIC:
- When the snake head comes within 2.0 units of the amber model, mark it as 'collected'. Hide the amber model and its point light. Increment a collection counter. After 2 seconds, respawn the amber at a new random position within (-20..20, 0.5, -20..20) and show it again.

STATE MANAGEMENT:
- Expose window.__3D_STATE__ updated every frame with:
  - segmentCount: number of snake segments (20)
  - headPosition: {x, y, z} of the head segment
  - heading: current heading angle in radians
  - headingDegrees: heading converted to degrees
  - speed: current movement speed
  - amplitude: current wave amplitude
  - paused: boolean
  - frameCount: number of animation frames elapsed (when not paused)
  - segmentPositions: array of {x, y, z} for all 20 segments
  - amberPosition: {x, y, z} of the amber model
  - amberVisible: boolean (whether amber is currently visible/not collected)
  - distanceToAmber: distance from head to amber
  - collectCount: number of times amber has been collected
  - wavePhase: current wave phase value
  - initialized: true after first frame
  - modelLoaded: boolean indicating if GLB loaded successfully
physics_constraints: Snake segments must maintain plausible spacing (0.5-1.2 units between consecutive segments). The sinusoidal wave must propagate tail-ward (phase increases with segment index). Head position must change continuously when not paused and speed > 0. All segment positions must remain NaN-free. Speed must stay clamped within [0.5, 8.0]. The snake must remain on the ground plane (Y near 0 for all segments).
